replacements.text: The acceptance-criteria standard's coverage rule asks whether a commitment has a criterion at all. Another rule's reviewer filed coverage gaps under it because of the same question in its opening sentence. That rule now asks only about each criterion's check. 9 of 10 reviewer panel runs on the corrected control document now return an empty report, up from 2 of 10. All 10 runs on the defective document still object to the planted criterion.
Every existing attack record's fingerprint changes because of the rule text in each emitted prompt.
Every specification reviewed against the deployed standard, in every project.
The owner, through a mistaken belief in a quieter panel.
Ten runs per document used the same model and effort. The one remaining control objection cites a flaw present in both document versions.

The `verification-contract` rule (the rule for judging each criterion's check) opened with the coverage rule's question. It now opens by judging each criterion's own check. It sends the question of a commitment having a criterion to coverage.
The instructions for running the reviewer panel gain a column in their reviewer table. The column names each reviewer's reading unit. That unit decides rule ownership.

The `verification-contract` rule opened with a requirement for a feasible check for every material commitment. Its reviewer filed coverage gaps under `verification-contract` because of that coverage question. 18 of 20 runs on the pilot's second case raised such objections under the original rule.

Each reviewer in the panel is defined by its reading unit. One examines a single criterion's form. One checks the set against the document's promises. One checks the set against itself. One examines a single criterion for untested cases. That unit decides rule ownership. Two reviewers may share ground through their different views of a criterion and the set.

The measurement used the pilot's second case and a corrected control. The second case is a realistic document of eight criteria with one planted defect. Ten fresh runs per document read prompts emitted from each version of the standard. 10 of 10 defective runs objected to the planted criterion under the planted rule, before the change and after it. 1 of 10 defective runs objected elsewhere, down from 10 of 10. 9 of 10 control runs returned an empty report, up from 2 of 10. The one remaining control objection cites a contradiction present in both versions of the test document.

No reviewer prompt changed. No existing attack record is reopened because of the record check's binding to the document's revision and never to the rule text. Other sentences in the panel's instructions were shortened to keep the instructions under the size cap.
The `verification-contract` rule judges each criterion's named check for feasibility and completeness. It sends the question of a commitment having a criterion to coverage.
The instructions for running the reviewer panel state each reviewer's reading unit beside the reviewer table.
At least 8 of 10 control runs come back empty. At least 8 of 10 defective runs object to the planted criterion.

One rule in the acceptance-criteria standard opened with the coverage rule's question. Its reviewer filed coverage gaps under it because of that overlap. Only 2 of 10 runs on the corrected control document came back empty.

The verification-contract rule (the rule for judging each criterion's check) now opens by judging each criterion's named check. The question of a commitment having a criterion at all stays with the coverage rule. The instructions for running the reviewer panel name each reviewer's reading unit in the reviewer table. That unit decides rule ownership.

make ci exits 0. 9 of 10 control runs returned an empty report in the pilot's second case, with ten runs per document. 10 of 10 runs detected the planted defect. One prose review round came back clean.
